**CENTRAL CONTRIBUTION:**
This work presents "Claws of Fate," a 2D adventure serious game developed in Unity that integrates a customized AI-based guide, BiomesAI, using OpenAI's ChatGPT and Azure Speech Studio to deliver real-time, context-specific educational content via text and audio about Brazilian biomes (Amazon Rainforest and Caatinga). The central contribution is the design, implementation, and initial user experience evaluation of this game, demonstrating how generative AI can be integrated into educational games to foster awareness of animal welfare, ethical pet care, and environmental conservation, particularly for early adolescents.

**PROBLEM AND CONTEXT:**
Adventure games hold significant educational potential for promoting environmental conservation and biodiversity awareness, especially by connecting animal care to broader ecological contexts. While existing digital games address these themes, there's a need for more engaging and cognitively stimulating tools for adolescents that bridge virtual experiences with real-world awareness. A promising direction is the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a personalized in-game assistant to guide players through ecosystems and enrich the experience with contextual knowledge. This paper addresses the gap in combining narrative, player action, and AI-simulated environmental responses to provide personalized and guided environmental education.

**METHOD/SYSTEM:**
Claws of Fate is a 2D adventure game developed using the Unity (2022.3.x) engine, targeting players with prior experience in reflex-based platformers, specifically early adolescents (represented by the 15-year-old protagonist, Peter). The game is set across two primary Brazilian biomes, the Amazon Rainforest and Caatinga, connected by a central Hub. The narrative follows Peter's quest to find his cat, Violet, after neglecting her, leading him through magical portals to explore biomes and learn about animal welfare and environmental conservation.

Gameplay involves event-based mechanics such as movement, jumping, dashing, and two biome-specific power-ups: a frog-inspired double-jump ability acquired in the Amazon Rainforest and a snake-inspired "fast forward" ability for quick movement through narrow spaces gained in the Caatinga. Players must collect three favorite items for Violet (yarn, fish, and milk) and scattered trash in each biome to activate exit portals. Each biome features native fauna and flora, with both supportive elements (e.g., capybaras, macaws) and hazards (e.g., piranhas, cacti, scorpions). The Hub serves as a central area for managing progress, revisiting biomes, and interacting with the AI guide.

The core innovation is BiomesAI, an integrated system providing contextual, on-demand educational content about the biomes' fauna and flora. BiomesAI utilizes OpenAI’s ChatGPT for generating textual content and Azure’s Speech Studio for converting text to audio. Its modular architecture comprises four main components: an AI Manager (coordinates game-AI communication), a Content Generator (sends prompts to ChatGPT), a Local Cache (stores responses to reduce latency and API calls), and a Resource Handler (manages content saving/loading). Supporting modules include OpenAIResponse for formatting ChatGPT outputs and BiomesData for content storage. A support library, Nuvia, manages backend connections to ChatGPT.

BiomesAI’s content generation employs a controlled prompt structure: a system prompt "You are an expert in Brazilian geography and biology. Specifically, you are knowledgeable about Brazilian biomes, their fauna, and flora," and a user prompt "Describe, in one to two paragraphs, {term}." To ensure content safety and age-appropriateness, real-time ChatGPT queries are disabled in the release version; all educational material is preloaded from a predefined JSON file (Predefined.json) and pre-approved. Audio responses are pre-generated using Azure’s Speech Studio with high-quality Portuguese female voices, selected for their perceived welcoming nature by young people, and integrated via standard Unity tools. The system's operation involves three stages: Preparation (Unity integration with OpenAI access key and curated content), Content Generation (developer-focused scene for generating and pre-approving texts), and In-Game Usage (retrieving educational responses from the local cache upon player interaction with environmental elements). Performance tests for AI models showed GPT-4 was the slowest (>10s, 31 tokens/s), while GPT-3.5 Turbo (≈70 tokens/s) and GPT-4o (≈89 tokens/s) were faster, leading to the adoption of GPT-4o and GPT-3.5 Turbo for pre-generation tasks to prioritize responsiveness and fluid gameplay.

**RESULTS AND METRICS:**
A user experience evaluation was conducted with 20 young adults (aged 20-23, predominantly male, experienced players), who completed a full gameplay session and responded to a multi-instrument UX questionnaire. This evaluation combined established models such as AttrakDiff, Game Experience Questionnaire (GEQ), Post-Study System Usability Questionnaire (PSSUQ), User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ), Curve, NASA-TLX, and adapted Microsoft Desirability Toolkit methods, complemented by Open-Ended Feedback.

Average scores (on a 1-5 Likert scale) revealed generally positive perceptions. The visual design (Q4) received the highest average score of 4.21, indicating strong aesthetic appeal. However, the usefulness of the in-game AI guide (Q14) scored lowest at 2.57, suggesting players were uncertain about interactive elements and focused on rapid progression to rescue Violet. Player-perceived influence on the narrative (Q8) scored 3.07, indicating limited agency due to the game's linear structure. Soundtrack immersion (Q11) scored 3.36, and overall difficulty (Q12) was rated 3.29. Other questions, covering AI information clarity, positive message about animal care, immersion, intuitive interface, clear navigation, smooth interaction, and relevant information, scored above 3.5.

Qualitative feedback from adjectives and open-ended suggestions provided further insights. The most frequent adjectives chosen were Challenging (16 mentions), Frustrating (10), Fun (10), Interesting (10), Environmental (9), and Educational (8). Key friction points included players overlooking interactive objects for the AI guide, a significant lack of checkpoints leading to frustration and forced level restarts, and abrupt/disorienting camera movement. Suggestions included more in-game hints and clearer cues for AI guide usage. Some test sessions experienced inactive audio, potentially impacting soundtrack evaluations.

**LIMITATIONS:**
The linear progression of the narrative inadvertently limited players' perceived agency, reflected in the low score for narrative influence (3.07). The urgency to rescue the cat, Violet, often led players to overlook optional interactive elements related to the AI guide, resulting in its low perceived usefulness (2.57). The absence of checkpoints was a major source of frustration, forcing players to restart entire levels upon failure. Camera movement was criticized for being abrupt and disorienting. Furthermore, relying on pre-generated AI content, while ensuring safety and control, meant the system did not fully exploit the dynamic, real-time personalization potential of generative AI. Issues with inactive audio on some testing computers may have negatively influenced evaluations related to the soundtrack.

**KEY CONCEPTS:**
Serious game, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Generative AI, OpenAI ChatGPT (GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4, GPT-4o), Azure Speech Studio, Unity Engine, Brazilian Biomes (Amazon Rainforest, Caatinga), Animal Welfare, Environmental Conservation, User Experience (UX) Evaluation, Platformer game mechanics, Multi-instrument evaluation (AttrakDiff, Game Experience Questionnaire, PSSUQ, UEQ, Curve, NASA-TLX, Microsoft Desirability Toolkit).
